title.en: Tabulation and the parts of a table

body.en: *Tabulation* is the systematic arrangement of classified data in rows and columns. It simplifies data, saves space, makes comparison easy and helps analysis. Classification comes first; tabulation presents the classified data. A table has: table number, title, head note (units), captions (column headings), stubs (row headings), body (the figures), footnote and source note.
body.kn: ಕೋಷ್ಟಕೀಕರಣ ಎಂದರೆ ವರ್ಗೀಕೃತ ದತ್ತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ಸಾಲು ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಲಂಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತವಾಗಿ ಜೋಡಿಸುವುದು. ಕೋಷ್ಟಕದ ಭಾಗಗಳು: ಕೋಷ್ಟಕ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ, ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆ, ಶಿರ ಟಿಪ್ಪಣಿ, ಕಾಲಂ ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆಗಳು (captions), ಸಾಲು ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆಗಳು (stubs), ಮುಖ್ಯ ಭಾಗ, ಅಡಿ ಟಿಪ್ಪಣಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂಲ ಟಿಪ್ಪಣಿ.

body.en: A simple or one-way table shows one characteristic (students by stream). A two-way table shows two characteristics together (students by gender and result). A manifold (higher-order) table shows three or more. *Tables* are also general-purpose (reference tables, e.g. Census tables) or special-purpose (summary tables for one study).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A college has 200 students: 120 boys and 80 girls. 90 boys and 60 girls passed. Prepare a two-way table.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A college has 200 students: 120 boys and 80 girls. 90 boys and 60 girls passed. Prepare a two-way table.
Boys failed equals 120 minus 90 equals 30; girls failed equals 80 minus 60 equals 20.
Total passed equals 90 plus 60 equals 150; total failed equals 30 plus 20 equals 50.
Row totals: 120 and 80; grand total equals 150 plus 50 equals 200 equals 120 plus 80. ✓.
So the answer is Pass: 90, 60, 150; Fail: 30, 20, 50; Totals: 120, 80, 200.
